findings.title: Route edit: use an in-modal sub-view that takes over the footer, and drop the extra confirm
findings.where: §8.3 Routes tab (Edit route, Forward to, + Redirect); shots v5-routes-edit-1280-light, v5-routes-confirm-1280-light; §13 Q2; round-6 backlog §1
findings.problem: v5-routes-edit shows 'Cancel edit / Save route' sitting straight above the modal footer's 'Cancel / Save'. That is two Cancels and two Saves in one view, which is why the top-of-tab note ('The page's Save button doesn't include them') has to exist at all. Adding a redirect takes three steps: the inline form with its live preview, the Add redirect button, then an alertdialog that repeats the preview word for word (v5-routes-confirm). The round-6 sub-view idea fixes this only if the sub-view also replaces the footer. If it slides only the tab body, the double Save is still there.
findings.fix: Spec one internal primitive (core/, three consumers: Edit route, Forward to, + Redirect). Its header is '← Routes' as Back, plus an h3 title. The tab strip is hidden or inert, and the modal footer is replaced by the sub-view's own footer (Cancel, Save route), so only one Save shows at a time. Escape and Back return to the tab. If the sub-form is dirty they first ask 'Discard route changes?', and only that sub-form is discarded. Unsaved page fields on other tabs are kept, and the tab's unsaved dot stays. Delete the top-of-tab note. Keep confirms only for destructive or wide-reaching actions: Delete route, Stop forwarding, and the cascade to child paths. The sub-view already shows the redirect and path-change consequences live, so Add redirect and a plain path change save directly. Browser Back while in the sub-view goes through NavigationGuard only when the sub-form is dirty. The sub-view is not put in the URL. This must be specced and mocked before the Routes work starts, and it is the only open question that blocks a phase.

findings.title: §12 build plan leaves out most of what v5 added
findings.where: §12 Phased plan table vs 'What changed in v5'
findings.problem: No phase contains the Routes tab rebuild, CwaUiTree, the routes list tree, the route sub-view, the modal conflict notice (§8.2), page status from routes (§9.3), the in-page CwaUiConfirm discard and leave flow (§8.5), or the 412 'Use Mia's / Keep mine' UI. Phase 6 names 'Confirm/Prompt' and 'list grid' but none of these. As written, the plan cannot be estimated or tracked against #236.
findings.fix: Add rows, or split phase 6 (see the next finding), so that every v5 headline item has a named PR: Tree + Routes tab + sub-view; conflict notice + 412 flow; list status from routes; discard and leave confirms with the NavigationGuard hook.

findings.title: Removals land before the ~220 site tabs are migrated
findings.where: §12 phases 4 and 6 vs phase 8; §1 principle 1 dev warning
findings.problem: Phase 4 removes RequestErrors and Notification. Phase 6 removes Modal*, DialogBox, Headless UI (and so today's public CwaUiSelect) and popper.ts. Phase 8, the last, migrates the template's and CK's tabs. Every site tab that uses those components breaks in the middle of the sequence, and the edge package publishes on every push to dev. The 'root is not CwaUiManagerTab' dev warning would also fire on all ~220 tabs as soon as it ships, so it would be ignored.
findings.fix: Move every removal into one late PR that runs after the template and CK are migrated, and keep old and new side by side until then. Turn the root warning on in that same PR. Each port PR adds its CHANGELOG line and a migration-note entry as it lands, so phase 8 is the codemod or checklist run, not the place notes get written.

findings.title: Editors see nothing until phase 3, and phase 2 ships store API with no consumer
findings.where: §12 phases 1–3; CLAUDE.md principle of least exposure
findings.problem: Phase 1 (tokens, bar frame, /kit) and phase 2 (fieldStates, the updateResource result, retry/reset, the NavigationGuard hook) change nothing an editor sees. Phase 2 also adds store getters and model methods whose only consumer arrives a PR later, which the project's least-exposure rule forbids. Phase 4 (toasts) depends only on tokens and replaces the RequestErrors and Notification pain directly, but it is scheduled after the field ports.
findings.fix: Re-sequence. (1) tokens, /kit, toasts. (2) a vertical slice: fieldStates + Field shell + Input/Toggle/Button/Select + the bar, using them in the module's own tabs. (3) Search with the API states. Then new controls, and so on. Every store addition then lands with its first consumer and test, and editors get toasts and a better bar within two PRs.

findings.title: Phase 6 is too large for one reviewable PR
findings.where: §12 row 6
findings.problem: One PR holds Dialog with tabs and the Save model, FormSection, FormGroup, Confirm and Prompt, the list grid, SearchField, FilterToggle, Pagination, ListState, Alert, Textarea and auth, plus four removals. Daniel reviews PRs before merge, and a PR this size will stall the plan or get reviewed thinly. It also needs a manual screen-reader pass across about 10 checklist rows at once.
findings.fix: Split it into: 6a Dialog + local-copy Save model + Alert + Confirm (§8.2, §8.5); 6b Routes tab + Tree + sub-view; 6c lists (grid, toolbar, filters, pagination, states, status from routes); 6d auth pages (3.3.8). The removals move to the late PR in the earlier finding.

findings.title: The per-PR bundle tracking column was dropped although many new reka-ui consumers arrive
findings.where: §12 intro (v4 04-proposal.md §11 had a 'new reka-ui consumers measured' column); §1 principle 9
findings.problem: v5 says only 'stating any bundle-budget change'. CLAUDE.md records that one extra reka-ui consumer already split popover into a chunk named in the entry's __vite__mapDeps, which costs visitors. The kit adds Combobox, AlertDialog, Popover (for every ⓘ, error and status), Toast, Tabs and Treegrid. Phase 2's fieldStates and the updateResource changes sit in ResourcesManager and the resources store, which are in the entry. CI skips the budget guards, so a regression can merge unnoticed.
findings.fix: Restore the column, naming the reka-ui primitives each PR first consumes. Require the test:e2e output (entry-bundle-markers, visitor-page-preloads) in each PR description. State up front that the fieldStates code must stay out of the entry, with getters in the store but write logic in a lazily loaded admin module, or budget for it explicitly.

findings.title: The updateResource result change breaks 28 callers that use the returned resource
findings.where: §8.4 'updateResource returns { ok: true } | { ok: false; error }'; §12 phase 2
findings.problem: Today `ResourcesManager.updateResource` returns the saved resource (resources-manager.ts:251, through versioned/sendUpdate), and 28 runtime files reference it. Changing it to `{ ok }` is a public breaking change and also loses the resource that callers such as useItemPage read. The plan does not count this work or the change for apps.
findings.fix: Return `{ ok: true; resource } | { ok: false; error }`, or keep the return value and expose the per-field error through fieldStates only. List the callers to update in phase 2's issue, and add a CHANGELOG line for apps that call it directly.

findings.title: Manual screen-reader passes on every PR are an unbudgeted cost
findings.where: §11.4 'manual VoiceOver (macOS and iOS) and NVDA (Windows) before each kit PR merges'; the browser scenario list
findings.problem: Three screen readers on two OSes for each of 8+ PRs (12+ after the splits) needs a Windows machine and an iOS device each time, plus a named person. The §11.4 browser list has about 30 measured scenarios at up to four widths in light and dark. No owner or time is set, so in practice this gets skipped or blocks merges.
findings.fix: Make axe, keyboard and the measurement checks on /kit the per-PR gate. These need no API rehearsal, because /kit uses fake models. Run the full VoiceOver/iOS/NVDA pass at three milestones: after the bar slice, after the modals (6a/6b), and before the migration PR. Keep rehearsal-backed browser scenarios for real flows only (the Save model, 412s, route actions).

findings.title: 'Template · 14 articles' and list gating need data the API may not send
findings.where: §9.3 status table; shots v5-list-*
findings.problem: I found no page-data count field in api-components-bundle/src (only internal counters in ComponentVoter and the fixture builder), so 'Template · 14 articles' needs a request per row or a bundle change. 'Held back by parent' per row needs each page's route with the admin-only _metadata.effectiveLiveAt in the list response. That should be confirmed before the list phase is scheduled.
findings.fix: Ship the list with a 'Template' badge and no count. File a bundle issue for a count, or a filter-total query, and add the number once it exists. Check that the pages collection embeds route liveAt and effectiveLiveAt for admins. Otherwise show only own-route status until it does.

findings.title: §13 still lists decided questions as open
findings.where: §13 Open questions 1–3
findings.problem: Round 6 approved Q1 (the palette) and Q3 (the treegrid), and the sub-view proposal replaces Q2. A developer picking up a phase cannot tell what still blocks.
findings.fix: Move Q1 and Q3 to 'Settled in v6' and replace Q2 with the sub-view spec as the single open item. State that it blocks only the Routes PR, and that phases 1–5 can start now.

result.routeFlowView: The sub-view is a good idea, with one condition: it must take over the modal footer as well as the tab body. In v5-routes-edit the trouble isn't the inline form. It's 'Cancel edit / Save route' stacked right above the modal's own 'Cancel / Save', which is also why the tab needs its explanatory note. A sub-view with the header '← Routes · Edit route' should hide or make inert the tab strip and replace the footer with its own Cancel and Save route. Then only one Save is ever on screen, the note can go, and no modal sits on top. Escape and Back return to the Routes tab, asking first only if the route form is dirty. Unsaved page fields on other tabs are kept, and their tab dot stays. The sub-view isn't put in the URL; browser Back goes through NavigationGuard only when the form is dirty. Build it once as an internal core/ primitive used by Edit route, Forward to and + Redirect. Because the sub-view shows the consequence live ('/kitchens/shaker will redirect here', '/old-kitchens will send visitors to …'), drop the confirm for adding a redirect and for a plain path change. Today that flow takes three steps and the confirm repeats the preview (v5-routes-confirm). Keep confirms for Delete route, Stop forwarding and the cascade to child routes. On phones it is the same sub-view filling the modal, with Back at the top-left. It should be specced and mocked before the Routes PR. Nothing else in the plan depends on it.

findings.title: Editing a route shows three Saves, two Cancels and two Deletes at once
findings.where: Spec §8.3 'Edit route, in place'; shot v5-routes-edit-1280-light (also -390)
findings.problem: In edit mode the tab shows Delete route / Cancel edit / Save route, and right under them the modal footer shows Delete page / Cancel / Save. A daily editor who changes the path will often press the footer's blue-looking Save, which is disabled or saves something else, and the route edit is lost when they close. A site owner cannot tell which Delete removes the page and which removes only the address. The tab's top note ('The page's Save button doesn't include them') asks the reader to work this out from a sentence.
findings.fix: Do this as the agreed sub-view (round-6 §1), not as an in-place edit. While the sub-view is open, hide the modal footer, or make it inert and visually recede, so Save route / Cancel are the only actions on screen. Move Delete route out of the form row into the sub-view header's ⋯ menu, or put it at the bottom under its own 'Danger' rule, so it never sits beside Save route.

findings.title: View on the sub-view proposal: yes, but define Back with unsaved input, header copy and the confirm on top
findings.where: round-6-backlog §1; spec §8.3, §8.5, §7 Escape order
findings.problem: The slide-in sub-view fixes the stacked-modal problem and the in-place reflow (in v5-routes-edit the Forwarding, Redirects and Child routes sections disappear without explanation). Three gaps remain. (a) Back or Escape after typing a new path is undefined, so either input is lost silently, which breaks §8.5's 'never dropped silently', or the behaviour is inconsistent. (b) The modal's tab strip stays visible, so pressing 'Details' mid-edit is another undefined exit. (c) Save route still opens a confirm dialog over the sub-view, which is the 'modal on top' Daniel wants to avoid.
findings.fix: Sub-view header: '← Routes' (Back), then an h3 'Edit route' / 'Forward to' / 'Add a redirect'. Back, Escape and a tab change with changed input ask 'Discard your route changes?' (Keep editing / Discard), using the §8.5 confirm; with nothing changed they leave at once. Hide or disable the modal tabs while the sub-view is open. Show the consequence the confirm would state inline in the sub-view, above the buttons ('/kitchens/shaker will redirect here', the cascade checkbox), and make Save route the confirmation itself, so no dialog stacks on the sub-view (see the next finding).

findings.title: Add redirect confirms what the form has just said
findings.where: Shot v5-routes-confirm-1280-light; mockup askConfirm 'Add a redirect from …?' (ui-kit.html ~3282)
findings.problem: The inline form already previews '/old-kitchens will send visitors to /kitchens/shaker.'. Pressing 'Add redirect' then opens a dialog saying the same sentence, with another 'Add redirect' button. An editor adding redirects after a site restructure clicks the same words twice per row and learns to click through confirms, which weakens the confirms that matter (Delete route, Forward). The decision 'each action after its own confirm' was made before the inline preview existed.
findings.fix: Keep a separate confirm only for destructive or hard-to-undo actions: Delete route, Delete redirect, Forward to, a path change. For additive actions whose form already shows the outcome (+ Redirect, + Route from a recommendation, go-live alone), the button press is the confirmation and a status line plus Undo follows. Put this to Daniel as a refinement of the decided rule, since it narrows it.

findings.title: 'Forwarding' and 'Redirects to this page' read as the same thing to a site owner
findings.where: Shot v5-routes-view-1280-light, sections 'Forwarding' and 'Redirects to this page'; Delete route confirm copy
findings.problem: Both sections are about sending visitors from one address to another, but in opposite directions, and only the section heading tells them apart. A non-technical owner who wants 'old address → this page' is as likely to press 'Forward to…', which hides the page from visitors entirely. The Delete route confirm's 'can only be reached through a page nested under it' is jargon, and it is wrong for a page with no children.
findings.fix: Rename the sections by outcome: 'Send visitors elsewhere' (button 'Send to another page…') and 'Old addresses that lead here' (button '+ Old address'). Make the Forward confirm's danger explicit: 'Visitors will no longer see this page.' as the first sentence, with the Forward button in a warning tone. Make the Delete route copy conditional: with no routed children, 'Visitors to /kitchens/shaker will get "Page not found".' only.

findings.title: Confirm's 'Cancel' sits over the form's own 'Cancel'
findings.where: Shot v5-routes-confirm-1280-light; askConfirm keep:'Cancel' for route, forward and redirect confirms
findings.problem: Three Cancels are on screen together: the confirm's, the inline redirect form's (visible behind the scrim) and the modal footer's. Each means something different: back to the form, abandon the redirect, discard the page edits. The §8.5 confirms use 'Keep editing', but the route confirms use 'Cancel'.
findings.fix: Route confirms name what staying means: 'Don't add', 'Don't delete', 'Keep forwarding off', or the 'Go back' used throughout. Never use a bare 'Cancel' in a confirm. With the sub-view, rename the sub-view's own Cancel to 'Back' or drop it, since Back already covers it.

findings.title: In the bar, 'Keep mine' silently overwrites Mia's saved value, and the popover repeats itself
findings.where: Spec §4.4 bar conflict; shot v5-conflict-bar-popover-390-light
findings.problem: The popover title 'Title: Mia changed this' is followed by the body line 'Mia changed this while you were editing.', so the same message appears twice in a small popover. More importantly, in the bar (which saves as you type), Keep mine saves immediately over a value Mia has already published or saved. In a modal, Keep mine only marks an unsaved choice. The same label does two different things and the bar copy doesn't say which.
findings.fix: Title the popover with the field and state only ('Title: changed by Mia') and keep the sentence, or the other way round, but not both. In the bar, label the buttons 'Use Mia's' and 'Save mine', so the immediate save is stated. Keep 'Keep mine' in modals, where nothing is sent until Save.

findings.title: '· Unsaved' label marker uses the link colour
findings.where: Shot v5-conflict-modal-390-light ('Reference · Unsaved', 'SEO page title · Unsaved'); spec §8.2
findings.problem: The marker is drawn in accent-fg blue, the token the spec reserves for links and 'Use this'. Beside the ⓘ button, editors will tap it expecting an action (show my change, undo). A site owner may also read blue as 'fine/info' rather than 'not saved yet'.
findings.fix: Draw '· Unsaved' in fg-muted with the same pending dot used on the tab and in the bar (dot + word), never in accent-fg. Reserve accent-fg for things that act.

findings.title: Phone list rows show two unlabelled dates side by side
findings.where: Shot v5-list-390-light: 'Scheduled · 20 Nov · 15 Nov · /ki…', 'Not live · 11 Nov · /our-workshop'; spec §9.1 'Below md'
findings.problem: On a scheduled row the go-live date and the meta date (last updated?) are next to each other with only a dot between. An editor checking 'when does this go live' can read 15 Nov. On other rows the lone date has no meaning attached either.
findings.fix: Below md, drop the meta date when the status already carries a date. Otherwise prefix it ('edited 15 Nov'). Same rule for templates ('Template · 14 articles · edited 16 Nov').

findings.title: Phone bar: the 'New' status glyph is a circled plus beside '+ Draft'
findings.where: Shot v5-cta-dots-new-390-light; spec §7 Phones (glyph per state: 'a circled plus for New')
findings.problem: With the status shown as a glyph only, a ⊕ button sits directly against the blue '+ Draft' button. Two plus signs read as two add actions. A site owner taps ⊕ expecting to add something and gets a status popover, or doesn't understand that '+ Draft' is the save.
findings.fix: Give New a non-plus shape, e.g. a dashed or hollow circle (not yet saved) or a small star. Keep plus signs exclusively for create actions.

findings.title: Phone Routes tab: Edit route splits the path from its recommendation, and 'Use this' wraps alone
findings.where: Shot v5-routes-failed-390-light (Route section)
findings.problem: At 390 the Edit route button drops between the path and 'Recommended: /kitchens/shaker-kitchens ·', and the separator dot is left dangling at the line end while 'Use this' wraps onto its own line. The recommendation looks unrelated to the path it replaces, and 'Use this' looks like a stray link.
findings.fix: Below sm, order the section as path + badge, then the recommendation line, then Edit route as a full-width button. Let 'Use this' wrap together with the path it applies to (a non-breaking group), with the separator dot inside the same group.

result.routeFlowView:
Go with the slide-in sub-view. It removes the stacked modal and fixes the worst part of v5: in v5-routes-edit the tab collapses to a form with no explanation, and three Save/Cancel/Delete sets compete with the modal footer. To make it work for a daily editor and an occasional owner:
(1) Header: '← Routes' as Back, then an h3 naming the task ('Edit route', 'Send visitors elsewhere', 'Add an old address').
(2) While the sub-view is open, hide or make inert the modal footer and the modal tabs, so Save route and Back are the only exits. Otherwise an editor presses the footer Save or switches tab and loses the route edit.
(3) Back, Escape and closing the modal with changed input ask 'Discard your route changes?', using the §8.5 confirm. With nothing changed they leave at once.
(4) Show the consequences inline in the sub-view, above the buttons: 'The old path /kitchens/shaker keeps working: it redirects here', the 'Also change the 2 child routes' checkbox, the redirect preview. Then Save route is the confirmation, and no dialog stacks on the sub-view. Keep a separate confirm only for Delete route, Delete redirect and Forward, which are destructive or hide the page.
(5) Delete route goes in the sub-view header's ⋯ menu or under a separate rule at the bottom, never beside Save route.
(6) On return, show the status line ('Route changed to …') at the top of the tab with focus on it, rather than on the trigger button: the trigger may not exist any more, for example after Delete route or + Route.
(7) Phone: the same sub-view full height inside the full-screen modal, with Save route sticky at the bottom where the modal footer was. This also fixes the cramped stacked Save/Cancel on phones.

results.title: Editing a route shows three Saves, two Cancels and two Deletes at once
results.evidence: v5-routes-edit-1280-light shows Delete route / Cancel edit / Save route above the modal footer's Delete page / Cancel / Save (disabled). So it is two Saves, not three; the title overcounts, but the problem is there. Round-6 §1 already moves editing to a sub-view and says its Save 'must not look like the modal's footer Save'. Hiding the footer and moving Delete route out of the row are not decided, and they are worth proposing.

results.title: View on the sub-view proposal: yes, but define Back with unsaved input, header copy and the confirm on top
results.evidence: Round-6 §1 sets out the slide, Back/Escape and focus, but does not say what Back, Escape or a tab change does after the user has typed. Spec §8.5 says unsaved changes are 'never dropped silently'. The confirm stacked on top is real: v5-routes-confirm shows an alertdialog over the tab. But round-5 §2 decided 'each with its own confirm', so making Save route the confirmation would re-open that decision and needs Daniel.

results.title: Add redirect confirms what the form has just said
results.evidence: ui-kit.html ~3133/3274 shows the live preview '<path> will send visitors to <path>.', and the confirm repeats it, as v5-routes-confirm shows. Round-5 backlog §2 records the decision that route actions are immediate, 'each with its own confirm'. The finding itself frames this as a refinement for Daniel to decide.

results.title: 'Forwarding' and 'Redirects to this page' read as the same thing to a site owner
results.evidence: Spec §8.3 (lines 580-581) and v5-routes-confirm show sections named 'Forwarding' and 'Redirects…'. The Delete route confirm (ui-kit.html 3254) always says '…can only be reached through a page nested under it', with no check for child routes. That is wrong for a page with none. The section naming is a judgement call; the unconditional copy is a concrete bug.

results.title: Confirm's 'Cancel' sits over the form's own 'Cancel'
results.evidence: v5-routes-confirm-1280-light shows the confirm's Cancel, the inline redirect form's Cancel behind the scrim, and the footer Cancel. ui-kit.html 3254 uses keep:'Cancel', while spec §8.5 confirms use 'Keep editing'. Nothing in the backlogs decides this label.

results.title: In the bar, 'Keep mine' silently overwrites Mia's saved value, and the popover repeats itself
results.evidence: The repetition is real: v5-conflict-bar-popover-390-light has the title 'Title: Mia changed this' and then the body line 'Mia changed this while you were editing.' The relabel to 'Save mine' conflicts with decisions already made: round-5 backlog (line 121) and spec §4.4 (line 357) fix 'Use Mia's' / 'Keep mine' for the bar and modals alike. Only the duplicated title is new.

results.title: '· Unsaved' label marker uses the link colour
results.evidence: Spec line 306: 'the label row adds "· Unsaved" in accent-fg, 600'. accent-fg is also the link colour (line 116) and the colour of inline text-button actions (line 337). v5-conflict-modal-390-light shows a blue '· Unsaved' beside the ⓘ. No backlog decision covers it.

results.title: Phone list rows show two unlabelled dates side by side
results.evidence: v5-list-390-light shows 'Scheduled · 20 Nov · 15 Nov · /ki…' and 'Not live · 11 Nov · /our-workshop'. Round-5 §4 defines the status words but not the meta date beside them.

results.title: Phone bar: the 'New' status glyph is a circled plus beside '+ Draft'
results.evidence: v5-cta-dots-new-390-light shows a ⊕ glyph right next to the blue '+ Draft'. Spec §7 (line 511) gives 'a circled plus for New'. Round-5 decided glyph-only with a distinct shape per state, but not which shape, so the choice can change.

results.title: Phone Routes tab: Edit route splits the path from its recommendation, and 'Use this' wraps alone
results.evidence: v5-routes-failed-390-light: the order is path + Live badge, then Edit route, then 'Recommended: /kitchens/shaker-kitchens ·' with the dot left at the line end and 'Use this' alone on the next line.

results.title: Route edit: use an in-modal sub-view that takes over the footer, and drop the extra confirm
results.evidence: Confirmed in v5-routes-edit-1280-light: 'Cancel edit / Save route' sits right above the footer's 'Cancel / Save', with the 'page's Save button doesn't include them' note at the top. v5-routes-confirm-1280-light: the alertdialog repeats the inline preview word for word. But some of the fix is already decided. Round-5 backlog §2 decided that route actions stay immediate 'each with its own confirm', and §8.3 keeps that. Round-6 §1 agrees the sub-view with its own Save route / Cancel, which 'must not look like the modal's footer Save', so it assumes the footer stays. Two parts are new and worth raising with Daniel: hiding or replacing the footer while the sub-view is open, and dropping the confirm for Add redirect and plain path changes.

results.title: §12 build plan leaves out most of what v5 added
results.evidence: In the §12 table, phase 6 lists Dialog, FormSection, FormGroup, Confirm/Prompt, list grid, SearchField, FilterToggle, Pagination, ListState, Alert and Textarea. No phase names CwaUiTree, the Routes tab rebuild or its sub-view, the modal conflict notice, or list status from routes. Phase 2 does mention useItemPage reporting per-field 412s, so the 412 flow is partly covered, but its UI is not. No backlog records a phase for these items.

results.title: Removals land before the ~220 site tabs are migrated
results.evidence: Most of the components removed in phases 4 and 6 are internal, not used by site tabs: DialogBox is core/DialogBox.vue, Modal* are core/admin/form/Modal*.vue, and RequestErrors and Notification are main/admin/header/_parts/. Site tabs use the public CwaUi* names. The only public one, CwaUiSelect, is ported in phase 3, before Headless UI goes in phase 6. Breaking changes are allowed in the alpha with a changelog line (01-requirements §194, memory 'No BC in alpha'). One part stands: the root warning from phase 1 would fire on every unmigrated tab until phase 8, but that is a minor point.

results.title: Editors see nothing until phase 3, and phase 2 ships store API with no consumer
results.evidence: §12 phase 2 adds fieldStates, the updateResource result and retry/reset, and their bar consumers (status glyph, BarSummary, Field) only arrive in phase 3. That goes against CLAUDE.md's least-exposure rule. Phase 2 does include useItemPage's per-field 422/412 reporting as a partial consumer. Phase 4 (toasts) needs only the tokens and still comes after the field ports. No backlog decides the order.

results.title: Phase 6 is too large for one reviewable PR
results.evidence: §12 row 6 really does put Dialog with tabs and the Save model, FormSection, FormGroup, Confirm/Prompt, the list grid, SearchField, FilterToggle, Pagination, ListState, Alert, Textarea and auth together with four removals in one PR. Nothing in round 5 or 6 settles how phases are sized.

results.title: The per-PR bundle tracking column was dropped although many new reka-ui consumers arrive
results.evidence: 04-proposal.md line 586-588 has the 'reka-ui consumers measured' column. 05 §12 says only 'stating any bundle-budget change'. CLAUDE.md records that a second reka-ui consumer split popover into a chunk named in the entry's __vite__mapDeps. Memory 'Run e2e for entry code' confirms that CI skips the budget guards. ResourcesManager is in the entry (CLAUDE.md, Bundle section).

results.title: The updateResource result change breaks 28 callers that use the returned resource
results.evidence: §8.4 says 'updateResource returns { ok: true } | { ok: false; error }'. Today it returns sendUpdate's result (resources-manager.ts ~251-262). The count '28' is inflated: 28 files mention updateResource including specs, but only 12 are non-spec files. About 5 of those use the return value: cwa-resource-model.ts:177, stranded-component-groups.ts:216, remote-changes.ts:296, clone-component.ts:65 and useItemPage.ts:167. So the break is real and the fix applies, but at a smaller scale than stated.

results.title: Manual screen-reader passes on every PR are an unbudgeted cost
results.evidence: §11.4 and the v5 change list do require 'manual VoiceOver (macOS and iOS) and NVDA (Windows) check before each kit PR merges'. The round-5 backlog §1, 'agreed with Daniel', records 'a manual VoiceOver/NVDA check before each kit PR merges', so per-PR passes are already decided. Splitting them into milestones would re-open that decision. The cost concern is legitimate, but it is for Daniel to revisit.

results.title: 'Template · 14 articles' and list gating need data the API may not send
results.evidence: Round-5 §4 and §9.3 decided the display, but not where the data comes from. A grep of the bundle's src turns up no page-data count per template. effectiveLiveAt appears only in RouteNormalizer and RouteLiveResolver, on Route itself, and I found nothing showing that the pages collection embeds it. So the concern holds: confirm the data before the list phase. The badge text itself is decided.

results.title: §13 still lists decided questions as open
results.evidence: §13 still lists Q1 (palette), Q2 (route edits) and Q3 (treegrid) as open. Round-6 backlog 'Decided on round 5' approves the palette and the treegrid, and §1 replaces Q2 with the sub-view. This is already recorded in the round-6 backlog, so v6's normal update would fix §13. It is real but expected bookkeeping.

findings.title: Route edit puts a second Cancel/Save row directly above the modal's footer
findings.where: §8.3 Edit route; shots v5-routes-edit-1280-dark, v5-routes-edit-390-light
findings.problem: In edit mode the tab shows 'Delete route · Cancel edit · Save route', and directly under it the footer shows 'Delete page · Cancel · Save'. The two rows have the same layout: a red text action on the left, then a soft button and a blue button on the right. The only thing that tells them apart is the word 'route', so 'which Save do I press' is a real risk. At 390 the Save route row touches the sticky footer with no gap. The edit state also quietly hides the Forwarding, Redirects and Child routes sections, so it is already a sub-view, just without a Back.
findings.fix: Make Edit route, Forward to and + Redirect a sub-view that slides in inside the modal. While the sub-view is open, its own footer (Delete route on the left, Cancel and Save route on the right) replaces the modal footer in the same sticky slot, so only one Save is ever on screen. See routeFlowView.

findings.title: Soft buttons use the same fill as fields, so actions look like inputs
findings.where: §2.1 field token, §5.1 soft variant; v5-routes-view-1280-light, v5-modal-sections-1280-light/dark
findings.problem: 'soft = field fill' made sense with the old pale fill. Now that the fill is #d6d3d1 (light) and #57534e (dark), Edit route, Forward to…, + Redirect and Cancel are the same grey block as a text input. In the Routes view, 'Edit route' sits on the path's line and reads as an empty field beside a read-only value. In the footer, Cancel looks like an input.
findings.fix: Give soft buttons their own token so they no longer share the field fill: `button-soft` stone-200 #e7e5e4 (light) and stone-700 #44403c (dark), with label weight 500, and `field-hover` on hover. Fields keep the darker fill, so the fill always means 'type here'. Check that its text reaches 4.5:1 (stone-900 on stone-200 does, and so does stone-100 on stone-700).

findings.title: A section action on the heading line spoils the heading rhythm
findings.where: Routes tab sections Forwarding and Redirects to this page (§8.3, §2.4 section-head); v5-routes-view-1280-light, v5-routes-saved-1280-dark
findings.problem: A 2.75rem soft button on the heading row makes the row tall. 'Forwarding' ends up about 3rem from 'Visitors see this page.', against the spec's 1rem from heading to content, so the heading floats nearer the rule above than the content it names. That reverses the rule of more space above than below. The Route section is different again: Edit route sits on the path line, not the heading line.
findings.fix: Use one placement for section actions: a compact control (2.25rem) set to the heading's line box with `align-self: center` and no extra block size, so the gap from heading to content stays 1rem. Or put actions after the section content, left-aligned. Use the same placement for Route, Forwarding and Redirects.

findings.title: The conflict diff is over-emphasised, looks like a link, and the light alert matches the field tint
findings.where: §8.2 conflict notice; v5-conflict-modal-1280-light, v5-conflict-bar-popover-1280-light
findings.problem: (a) The difference is shown with 650 weight, an underline and a tint at once. When the whole value differs ('Kitchens & worktops' / 'Our kitchens', and both SEO titles) every word is highlighted, so the highlight tells you nothing. (b) Underlined text is the kit's link style (§11.1), and the alert directly above uses underlined links. (c) In light, the modal alert's fill is almost the `field-warning` field fill (#dcc9ad), so the alert, the conflicting field and the notice read as three similar beige blocks. (d) The bar popover's title 'Title: Mia changed this' repeats in its first line, and its buttons are left-aligned where the modal's are right-aligned.
findings.fix: Mark the difference with tint and 650 weight only, with no underline. Leave out the highlight when more than about half the words differ. Give the modal alert the 10% warning surface plus the 3px start edge, as the notice has, rather than the field tint. Make the bar popover title 'Title: changed by Mia', drop the repeated line, and right-align its buttons as in the modal.

findings.title: Phone Routes view: the recommendation line breaks badly and Edit route splits path from recommendation
findings.where: §8.3 Route section on phones; v5-routes-failed-390-dark, v5-routes-edit-390-light
findings.problem: At 390 'Recommended: /kitchens/shaker-kitchens ·' wraps, leaving the '·' orphaned at the end of the line and 'Use this' alone on the next. In the view state, the Edit route button falls between the path and its recommendation, so the recommendation reads as belonging to the button.
findings.fix: Below a container width of about 25rem, drop the '·' and put 'Use this' on its own line as a text button with a 2.75rem hit area. Order the section as path and badge, then recommendation, then actions, at every width.

findings.title: The inline + Redirect form has its buttons the other way round and a confirm modal on top
findings.where: §8.3 + Redirect; v5-routes-confirm-1280-light
findings.problem: The inline form shows 'Add redirect' (solid) then 'Cancel'. The footer, Edit route and the confirm all put the secondary button first and the primary last. On top of that, the confirm is an alertdialog over the modal, which is exactly the modal-on-modal layering Daniel wants gone.
findings.fix: Move + Redirect into the sub-view as well (path input, live preview, Cancel then Add redirect in the sub-view footer). Use secondary then primary order in every button row.

findings.title: Phone toasts cover a full-screen dialog's header
findings.where: §10 toast position on phones; v5-routes-failed-390-dark, v5-cta-dots-live-390-light
findings.problem: On phones toasts sit at the top, below the admin header. A full-screen dialog covers the admin header, so the stack lands on the dialog's title and close ×. In routes-failed-390 the info toast hides 'Shaker kittchens' and the ×. The close button is then under a toast, which is the 2.4.11 situation the spec tries to avoid.
findings.fix: When a full-screen dialog is open, the toast region's fixed top is the bottom of the dialog's sticky header and tab strip. That is a fixed anchor per surface, so it does not break 'toasts never move'. State it in §10.

findings.title: Trash icons are always red in the tree
findings.where: §5.4 row actions; v5-routes-view-1280-light, v5-routes-saved-1280-dark
findings.problem: Every redirect row shows a solid red trash icon, so a column of three or four red glyphs is the loudest thing on the tab, louder than the section headings and the Live badges. `danger` should signal a destructive moment, not idle rows.
findings.fix: Show row action icons in `fg-muted` at rest, turning `danger-fg` with `step-hover` on hover or focus. The accessible name already says Delete.

findings.title: Three different 'more' glyphs
findings.where: §5.1 split button ⋮; §9.1 list rows ⋯; §5.4 tree ⋯; phone modal header ⋯ (v5-routes-edit-390-light, v5-list-1280-dark)
findings.problem: Daniel settled on ⋮ for the bar's 'More actions', but list rows, tree rows and the phone modal header use horizontal ⋯. The same meaning has two shapes across bar, modal and list.
findings.fix: Use the solid vertical ⋮ everywhere (row actions, tree, modal header) and update the §5.3, §5.4 and §9.1 copy.

findings.title: Phone list status line has a ragged start, and Scheduled can be confused with Static
findings.where: §9.1 below md, §9.3; v5-list-390-light, v5-list-1280-dark phone frame
findings.problem: On the second line, 'Held back by parent' renders with no visible dot, and template rows have no dot, so the line starts at three different x positions down the list. Scheduled uses a blue (accent) circle on line two while the Static type marker is a blue circle on line one, so the same hue and shape mean two things in one row.
findings.fix: Always render a fixed 0.75rem status slot on line two: the coloured dot, or for templates a neutral hollow square, so text always starts at the same x. Give Scheduled a clock glyph, matching the bar's Scheduled shape, instead of an accent dot.

result.routeFlowView:
I support the sub-view, and it should replace the footer, not only the panel. The mockup already half-does it: in edit mode the other sections disappear, but the tab strip and the modal footer stay, so two Save rows end up stacked. Proposal:

1. Structure. The modal header (title, ×) stays. The tab strip is replaced, in the same 2.75rem slot so the body does not jump, by a sub-view header: a '‹ Routes' back button (ghost, 2.75rem hit area) and the sub-view's h3 ('Edit route', 'Forward to', 'Add a redirect'). The tabs come back on return. The modal footer swaps to the sub-view's footer in the same sticky slot: destructive on the left (Delete route, only in Edit route), Cancel then Save route / Forward / Add redirect on the right. Only one Save is ever visible, which answers 'must not look like the modal's Save' by never showing both. If the page has unsaved field changes, the sub-view footer shows a muted 'Page changes kept' text and nothing is lost.

2. Confirms. The sub-view is already a deliberate review step, so the alertdialog on top can go. The consequences go inline above the footer instead: 'The old path /kitchens/shaker will redirect here', the 'Also change the 2 child routes…' checkbox, and 'Visitors to /old-kitchens will be sent to …'. That gets rid of the remaining modal-on-modal (v5-routes-confirm). It touches the round-5 decision 'each with its own confirm', so Daniel should confirm it. Keep a confirm only for Delete route, and show it inline in the sub-view rather than as a dialog.

3. Return. On a successful save, slide back, show the status line in the section that changed (not a full-width alert at the top of the tab as in v5-routes-saved), flash the new or changed row once, and return focus to the button that opened the sub-view. On failure, stay in the sub-view with the danger alert and Retry in the sub-view, keeping what was typed.

4. Escape order. Insert the sub-view into §7's list before the dialog: popover or menu, then sub-view (Back, asking 'Discard this route change?' only if the sub-form is dirty), then dialog.

5. Motion. Inside a 36rem modal, a full-width slide is a lot. Use translateX(2rem) plus a fade, 200 ms with --ease-out, the reverse on Back, instant under reduced motion. Reset the body's scroll to the top on entering and restore it on Back.

6. Phone. The same structure. The sub-view header takes the tab strip's place under the dialog title, and the sub-view footer uses the 50/50 phone footer layout. Delete route moves to the sub-view header's ⋮, as the modal's destructive action does.

7. One pattern. Use the same CwaUiDialogSubview for Edit route, Forward to and + Redirect, and later for any drill-in inside a modal, so it becomes a kit component rather than a one-off for Routes.

findings.title: Tab metadata resolver mounts every tab's field tree off-screen, so field="…" inputs will misfire
findings.where: §1 / §8.4 ("Unmounting a field in error or held raises a persistent toast"), §4.3 portalled flags; today's src/runtime/templates/components/core/useDataResolver.ts
findings.problem: ResourceManager reads each tab's name and order by rendering the whole tab with `render(vnode, detachedDiv)` and then `render(null)` on every selection change. With `field="…"`, each kit input creates its own `useCwaResourceModel` inside that throwaway render, so it registers a model editor (a 412 or remote change can reach a hidden instance), tries to teleport a presence flag into a layer that isn't there (Vue warns once per field), and unmounts straight away. Under §8.4 that unmount fires the "field in error" toast for every tab whose field is in error, each time the editor selects something. Today it only creates the tab's own setup models; the kit makes it create every field.
findings.fix: Spec a metadata-only mode. ResourceManager's resolver provides a `cwaTabMetaOnly` key, and `CwaUiManagerTab` renders no slot content when it is set. The dev check for a missing `CwaUiManagerTab` root moves into the resolver, which can see `subTree.type`. Add a Vitest case: selecting a resource with a tab whose field is in error raises no toast and mounts no model.

findings.title: The either/or group and LinkInput have three conflicting APIs, and none can send a single save
findings.where: §1 example (`<CwaUiLinkInput :fields="['route','rawPath']">`), §6.1 (`CwaUiEitherOr :iri` with children taking `:model`), §6.3 (`route?`/`rawPath?` rename props), §6.2 "one updateResource"
findings.problem: The spec names LinkInput's fields three different ways. §6.1 also takes `:iri`, which contradicts the rule that `field` reads its IRI from the tab. §6.2 needs one PATCH that carries the chosen field plus nulls for the others, and an Undo that restores both. Each child, though, owns a separate `useCwaResourceModel` with its own debounce, and today `property: string[]` means a nested path, not several fields. Today's LinkTab.vue shows the result: it writes `rawPath = null` through a second model as a separate request.
findings.fix: Pick one form: `<CwaUiLinkInput field="route" alt-field="rawPath">`, or `:fields` everywhere, and drop `:iri` from EitherOr inside a tab. Specify a group model, for example an internal `useCwaResourceFieldGroup(iri, fields[])`, that owns one debounce and one `updateResource` with the nulls, and that the options' inputs bind to. Give it its own `state` for the single status glyph, and put it in PR 5's row.

findings.title: The scope of field="…" is undefined outside the bar and missing from the binding rules
findings.where: §1 point 1, §3 table, §4.1 ("A control takes :model or v-model, never both"), §8.2
findings.problem: `field` is the third binding mode, but §4.1's exclusivity rule and dev warning cover only `:model` and `v-model`. The spec never says where `field` gets its IRI: `ResourceManager` renders `<component :is=selectedTab class=…>` with no `iri` prop, and tabs read `resourceStackManager.currentIri`. It also never says what `field` means inside `CwaUiDialog` or `CwaUiFormGroup`, where fields must bind to `useItemPage`'s `localResourceData` and show "· Unsaved" and 422 errors. Nor does it say how a nested path (`seo.title`) maps to a `fieldStates` key, given that the model PATCHes the root property and a 422 `propertyPath` can be nested.
findings.fix: Add a §4.1a: `field` resolves against the nearest provider. Under `CwaUiManagerTab` (which injects `currentIri`) it makes a live model; under `CwaUiDialog` or `FormGroup` (which inject the local-copy API from `useItemPage`) it makes a local-copy field with `state` from that copy; with no provider it warns in development. The rule becomes "exactly one of `field`, `:model`, `v-model`". `fieldStates` keys are the full dotted path, and errors map by `propertyPath`. Test all three providers in Vitest.

findings.title: The routes edit screen stacks two Saves and two red Deletes; adopt the sub-view, but specify it
findings.where: shot v5-routes-edit-1280-light (Cancel edit / Save route above Delete page / Cancel / Save), §8.3, round-6-backlog §1, §7 Escape order
findings.problem: In the screenshot, "Delete route" sits directly above "Delete page", and "Save route" directly above a disabled "Save". The note at the top of the tab is the only thing that tells them apart. The round-6 sub-view proposal fixes this only if the modal footer goes while the sub-view is open. Today's RoutesTab.vue already switches screens (`currentScreen`, "< Back to Routes"), so the sub-view only formalises what exists. As written it leaves out Escape order, a dirty sub-view, switching tabs, browser Back and `inert`.
findings.fix: Add an internal `core/ui/SubView.vue` (one consumer only, so not a public `CwaUi` name). The header holds Back and an `h3` heading, which takes focus. Save route / Cancel sit in-body at the end of the sub-view. The modal footer is hidden while the sub-view is open, replaced by a muted line "3 page changes unsaved" when there are any. Escape order becomes: confirm, popover or menu, sub-view (asks "Discard changes to the route?" when dirty), modal. Switching tabs closes the sub-view and asks the same when it is dirty. The sub-view never pushes router history. The off-screen panel gets `inert`. Browser scenario: Back and Escape return focus to Edit route, and the modal's Save never shows beside Save route.

findings.title: The §4.1 contract doesn't match today's useCwaResourceModel return, and the glyph's data source is ambiguous
findings.where: §4.1 `ResourceModelField`, §4.2 ("FieldStatus … reads only its field's state"), §8.4 "read from the resources store"; src/runtime/composables/cwa-resource-model.ts
findings.problem: Today the model returns `{ states: { pendingSubmit, submitting, isBusy, isLongWait }, resetValue, model, localValueWithIri, remoteChange, focus, blur, focusedBy, focusListeners }`, with no `iri`, `field`, `state`, `retry` or `reset`. The spec doesn't say the return changes, whether `states` stays, or that `:model` takes the whole object rather than `title.model`. It also says the glyph reads both `model.state` and the store by `(iri, field)`. If FieldStatus reads the store, /kit's fake models (§12) can't show states without seeding Pinia. `state` is also another nested ComputedRef (#260) that authors will read in templates.
findings.fix: Say that PR 2 changes the return to §4.1's shape, with a migration line (`states.isBusy` becomes `state.value.status === 'saving'`, `resetValue` becomes `reset`). Kit components read only `props.model.state`, and only the model reads the store. Add a dev warning when `:model` receives a Ref instead of the model object. Add `state` to CLAUDE.md's #260 destructure list.

findings.title: The v5 catalogue is too thin to build or test from
findings.where: §5.1–§5.4 versus 04-proposal.md §5 (SelectOption, Segmented `options`, `source`, `max`)
findings.problem: v5 dropped v1's prop types, and v1 is only "still applies" for the migration map. A builder has to merge two documents that disagree (`outline` versus `soft`). Several APIs are missing entirely: the `options` item shape for the split button (`label`, `onSelect` or `value`, `disabled`, `reason`, `tone`, groups); `icon` (component or name?); `tone` values; emits and slots for any control; CwaUiTree's data shape (`id`, `label`, `badge`, `children`, `actions`, lazy loading?); and ResourceSearch's `endpoint`, the label and secondary-line property names, and the query parameter (#328's `search`).
findings.fix: Make §5 self-contained, with one typed block per public component listing props, emits, slots and exposed members, written as TypeScript interfaces, so PR specs and `/kit` cases come straight from it. Mark everything v1 defined that v5 keeps.

findings.title: New entry-chunk code isn't planned against the bundle budget
findings.where: §8.4 (`fieldStates` actions, eviction guard), §10 `useCwaToast()`, §11.2 announcer, §8.5 `NavigationGuard`/`beforeunload`, §12 PR rows
findings.problem: The resources store, the route-cache eviction code, `Admin` and `NavigationGuard` all sit in the entry, which CLAUDE.md says has a few bytes of headroom. §8.4 adds actions there (move on IRI change, retry/reset, the eviction check). `useCwaToast` is auto-imported into apps' pages, so a static import of the Toaster or reka toast drags admin code into visitors' preloads. Each new reka consumer has already split reka chunks into the entry's `__vite__mapDeps` (#416), and the kit adds about 20.
findings.fix: Keep only the `fieldStates` state key in the store. Put its getters and actions in an admin module loaded with `lazyImport`, the way clone-mode does. `useCwaToast` is a stub that queues and `import()`s the Toaster, which is an async component mounted only for admins. The announcer lives in lazy admin code. Each §12 row lists `entry-bundle-markers` and `visitor-page-preloads` as gates with a budget delta, and PR 1 records the reka chunk count as a baseline.

findings.title: The dev warning lands in PR 1 but tabs migrate in PR 3 to PR 8
findings.where: §12 PR 1 (`CwaUiManagerTab` and its warning), §1 ("A tab whose root is anything else gets a development warning"), §3 (`CwaUiTextarea` under bar "throws in development")
findings.problem: From PR 1 every module tab (DynamicPage, Publish, Group, Info, Ui, Order, ported in PR 3) and every app tab (template, CK, ported in PR 8) warns each time it is selected. They can't migrate yet, because LinkInput, FileUpload and Number arrive in PR 5 and PR 7. Throwing in development from a child of the bar also kills the whole bar render, not just the textarea.
findings.fix: Ship `CwaUiManagerTab` in PR 1 without the warning. Turn the warning on in the PR that ports the module tabs, and for apps in PR 8, warning once per component definition. A `CwaUiTextarea` under the bar logs an error and renders nothing in both modes.

findings.title: The bar's live region can't belong to CwaUiManagerTab
findings.where: §3 table (surface `bar` "Provided by `CwaUiManagerTab`"), §11.2 "One region per surface"
findings.problem: `CwaUiManagerTab` unmounts when the editor switches tabs or the selection changes, and saves outlive both: §11.2 merges outcomes within about 1 s and announces a slow "Saving…". A region owned by the tab disappears mid-message, and two tab instances during a switch would mean two regions. BarSummary and the tab badges also read state across tabs.
findings.fix: The surface context (live region, announcer queue, flag layer, `surface: 'bar'`) is provided by `ResourceManager`/`BarSummary`. `CwaUiManagerTab` only injects it, lays out the row and adds the IRI scope. Vitest: switch tabs while a save is in flight and assert that one merged announcement still arrives.

findings.title: /kit needs a fake-model factory and page meta to be testable
findings.where: §12 "The kit reference page", §11.4 "browser tests open /kit"
findings.problem: The spec doesn't say how `/kit` builds "fake models fixed in every state". Without a shared factory, `/kit` and the Vitest specs will each write their own fakes and drift apart. A playground page also runs CWA's route middleware and auth unless it opts out, so the replay-only browser tests would need a recorded rehearsal for `/kit`. Kit pieces gated on `isAdmin` (the realtime view, presence flags) render nothing for an anonymous visitor.
findings.fix: Name an internal `fakeFieldModel(state)` factory, typed as `ResourceModelField` and used by both `/kit` and the Vitest specs. Give `kit.vue` `definePageMeta({ cwa: { disabled: true } })`, as `playground/app/pages/static.vue` does. State whether `/kit` signs in or injects an admin-shaped `$cwa`, so its browser scenario needs no API requests.

result.routeFlowView: Support Daniel's sub-view, with conditions. Today's RoutesTab.vue already switches screens (currentScreen, "< Back to Routes"), so this mostly formalises what exists. It is better than the v5 in-place edit, which in v5-routes-edit-1280-light stacks Cancel edit / Save route above Cancel / Save and puts "Delete route" directly over "Delete page". It is also better than a second dialog, which would mean nested focus traps and two scrims. The sub-view only fixes that confusion if the modal footer is hidden while it is open. Keep one muted line, "3 page changes unsaved", so the page's pending changes stay visible, and put Save route / Cancel at the end of the sub-view body rather than in a footer. Build it as an internal core/ui/SubView.vue, not a public CwaUi component, because the Routes tab is its only consumer (Edit route, Forward to, + Redirect). The header holds a Back button and an h3 heading, which takes focus on entry; leaving returns focus to the button that opened it. The slide is a 200 ms translate, instant under reduced motion, and the hidden panel gets `inert`. Add the sub-view to the Escape order between popover or menu and the modal. Back, Escape or switching tab with unsaved route edits asks "Discard changes to the route?". The sub-view never pushes router history, so browser Back still goes through NavigationGuard for the whole modal. The path-change confirm (with the cascade checkbox) stays an in-page CwaUiConfirm over the sub-view. That is a confirm, not another modal, so it fits Daniel's constraint. On phones it is the same panel, full height inside the full-screen modal, with the tab strip still visible.

results.title: Three different 'more' glyphs
results.evidence: Spec line 386: the split button uses ⋮ (decided, round-5-backlog line 90, about the split button only). Spec lines 457, 464, 582 and 647 use horizontal ⋯ for rows and the modal. The ⋯ appears in v5-routes-edit-390-light (modal header), v5-routes-view-1280-light (child routes) and v5-list-390-light (list rows). The rows were never decided, so the two glyphs are a real inconsistency.

results.title: Phone list status line has a ragged start, and Scheduled can be confused with Static
results.evidence: In v5-list-390-light, 'Held back by parent' is indented with no visible dot. Template rows start with no dot. Other rows start with a dot. So line two starts at different x positions. Scheduled shows a blue dot on line two (spec line 666, 'accent dot') while the Static marker is a blue circle on line one of the same row.

results.title: Tab metadata resolver mounts every tab's field tree off-screen, so field="…" inputs will misfire
results.evidence: src/runtime/templates/components/core/useDataResolver.ts renders each tab with h(definition, cProps) into a detached div via render(vnode, wrapper), then render(null, wrapper) in completeLoad, and does this again whenever the components or props change. That is a full subtree mount. Under spec §1, kit inputs with field="…" build their own models, and §8.4 says unmounting a field in error or held raises a persistent toast. Nothing in the spec or the backlogs covers a metadata-only render.

results.title: The either/or group and LinkInput have three conflicting APIs, and none can send a single save
results.evidence: §1 has <CwaUiLinkInput :fields="['route','rawPath']">. §6.1 has CwaUiEitherOr :iri="iri" with children taking :model="route". §6.3 says route?/rawPath? props rename the fields. §6.2 requires one updateResource carrying the nulls. playground/app/cwa/components/NavigationLink/admin/LinkTab.vue does use two separate useCwaResourceModel calls and nulls rawPath through the second model. Q7 decided the pattern, not this API, and §6 names no group model.

results.title: The scope of field="…" is undefined outside the bar and missing from the binding rules
results.evidence: §4.1 only says "A control takes :model or v-model, never both". §1 says field builds its model "from the tab's resource" and never says how. ResourceManager.vue renders <component :is="selectedTab" class="cwa:w-full"> with no iri. §8.2 and §558 put modal state in useItemPage's local copy, yet nothing says what field= does under CwaUiDialog or FormGroup, or how a nested path maps. round-5 §5 decided field= in the bar only.

results.title: The routes edit screen stacks two Saves and two red Deletes; adopt the sub-view, but specify it
results.evidence: Shot v5-routes-edit-1280-light confirms it: Delete route / Cancel edit / Save route sit directly above the footer's Delete page / Cancel / disabled Save. RoutesTab.vue already has currentScreen and '< Back to Routes'. The round-6 backlog §1 already proposes the sub-view with Back, Escape, focus handling and its own Save route that 'must not look like the modal's footer Save'. That covers the direction but not footer hiding, the dirty-sub-view confirm, tab switching, inert, or §7's Escape order. So the direction is planned, and the extra details here are new.

results.title: The §4.1 contract doesn't match today's useCwaResourceModel return, and the glyph's data source is ambiguous
results.evidence: cwa-resource-model.ts returns { states:{pendingSubmit,submitting,isBusy,isLongWait}, resetValue, model, localValueWithIri, remoteChange, focus, blur, focusedBy, focusListeners }, with no iri, field, state, retry or reset. The §4.1 interface differs and no migration is stated. §4.1 says CwaFieldState 'is read from the resources store' while §4.2 says FieldStatus 'reads only its field's state'. Both are ambiguous about the source, and §12 /kit relies on fake models. Round-5 decided only the model names in §8.4.

results.title: The v5 catalogue is too thin to build or test from
results.evidence: v5 §5.1 and §5.2 list props loosely, with no option item shape for split-button options, no CwaUiTree data shape (§5.4 has only look and ARIA), and no ResourceSearch props beyond endpoint in the §6.1 example. v1 (04-proposal.md lines 207–213) had SelectOption, source, max and ResourceSearch's endpoint, property and searchProperties, but §12 says only v1's migration map 'still applies'. The outline/soft clash is resolved by §12's migration note, so that part of the finding is weaker.

results.title: New entry-chunk code isn't planned against the bundle budget
results.evidence: §12 only says each PR states 'any bundle-budget change', and §1 principle 9 says 'Kit code is lazy and admin-only'. Neither says where fieldStates actions (§8.4, in the entry's resources store), the eviction guard, the NavigationGuard hook or the auto-imported useCwaToast (§10) go, or which entry and preload guards each PR must pass. CLAUDE.md records the entry headroom and the reka chunk split (#416). This is a planning gap rather than a contradiction.

results.title: The dev warning lands in PR 1 but tabs migrate in PR 3 to PR 8
results.evidence: §12 PR 1 ships CwaUiManagerTab, and §1 and round-5 §5 say a dev warning names any tab whose root is not CwaUiManagerTab. Module tabs move 'on the row' in PR 3, while Number, LinkInput and FileUpload come in PR 5 and app tabs in PR 8. The spec never says when the warning is switched on. §3 says CwaUiTextarea under bar 'throws in development'. The warning itself is decided; its timing and the throw are not.

results.title: The bar's live region can't belong to CwaUiManagerTab
results.evidence: The §3 table says surface bar is 'Provided by CwaUiManagerTab'. §11.2 asks for one region per surface with merged, delayed announcements. ResourceManager.vue renders the tab through <component :is="selectedTab">, so it unmounts on a tab switch. Round-5 decided one region per surface but not who owns it.

results.title: /kit needs a fake-model factory and page meta to be testable
results.evidence: §12 and round-5 §11 say only 'fake models fixed in every state' and that browser tests open /kit. There is no shared factory, no definePageMeta({ cwa: { disabled: true } }) (which playground/app/pages/static.vue uses) and no word on admin identity. CLAUDE.md's browser-test replay fails any unrecorded request. This is a minor specification gap.
